title: Prove a delay before claiming it
statement: Call a check delayed only when the time that passed is recorded and proves the delay, because success on the same day shows short-term memory, not learning.
example: A unit planned a 24-hour delay before its checkpoint, but the platform did not enforce it and no elapsed time was captured.
detail: A demo reading unit's 90% gate was verified, but the platform did not enforce the intended 24-hour delay and no elapsed-time evidence was captured, so it is not a verified delayed assessment (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/handoffs-2026-07-13/course-eval-layer/README.md`). The practice spec licenses "acquired at checkpoint" and adds "delayed" only when timestamp evidence proves the interval, and never counts release-day completion, since same-day testing measures working memory, not learning (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/practice-layer-spec.md`). It sharpens the rule that learning needs a later test on new items: the test has to be provably later.
